prerequisites: Knowledge of differential and integral calculus of single-variable functions

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering related to: complex variable, integral calculus in several variables and differential equations.
Basic knowledge of computer programs with application in engineering.
Knowledge of basic subjects and technologies, enabling students to learn new methods and technologies, as well as providing them with versatility to adapt to new situations.

Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities, understanding the ethical and professional responsibility of the activity of the Industrial Technical Engineer.
Propose and calculate integrals of functions of two and three variables and apply them to solving engineering problems.
Parameterize curves and surfaces with ease, perform integration of scalar and vector functions over them, and apply this to solving engineering problems.
Understand the basic properties of complex functions and be able to approximate them through series expansions.
Understand the essential qualitative aspects of differential equations: existence, uniqueness, and regularity of solutions.
Acquire proficiency in the explicit resolution of first-order and higher-order differential equations and relate the latter to first-order systems.
Understand the concept of partial differential equations.

teaching_methods: Laboratory practices (computer labs with software for calculations)
assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, the final grade (NF) is calculated as NF = 0.15*NL + 0.15*NA + 0.7*NC. If a student does not achieve a minimum grade of 4 out of 10 in NC, the final grade will be a fail, and the numerical grade in the record will be the minimum between the final grade (NF) and 4. For extraordinary calls, NF = 0.15*NL + max{0.15*NA + 0.7*NC, 0.85*NC}, where NC is the exam grade. Students who do not attend the ordinary exam will be marked as "No presentado". For differentiated assessment, students will be evaluated by a theoretical exam (85%) and a practical exam (15%).
